headlines.text: On a Wednesday in 2024, back when The Young Bucks vs. Fletcher & Ospreay clashed for the AEW World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.43 ? an excellent showing. Fletcher & Ospreay was challenging for gold for the very first time. Fletcher's dive-back interference helped Ospreay and the Young Bucks survive a TK Driver spot, with the Bucks retaining their tag titles over Ospreay and Fletcher in a Match of the Year contender.

Back on this day in 2024, Hook vs. Roderick Strong clashed for the FTW Title in a FTW Rules match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.54. It was the 20th time the FTW Title had been on the line, a nice marker in that championship's story. A hard-fought battle for the gold.

Rewind to 2024, when Jon Moxley vs. Darby Allin met in a Number One Contender, serving as the night's main event on Dynamite, rated 7.83 ? a good, competitive contest, on an outstanding Grand Slam '24 - Night 1 show that earned an overall rating of 8.34.

secondaries.text: It was 2024 when Mariah May vs. Yuka Sakazaki put the AEW Women's World Title on the line, appearing on Dynamite, rated 4.75. For Yuka Sakazaki, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. This stood as the 60th match in AEW Women's World Title history ? a genuinely rare milestone for that title.
Flash back to 2024, when Bryan Danielson vs. Nigel McGuinness delivered a fantastic contest on Dynamite, rated 8.06 ? part of a stacked Grand Slam '24 - Night 1 card, rated 8.34 overall.
